answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may transact: creating thousands of fake agents then means locking thousands of stakes, turning a cheap meadow of sockpuppets into an expensive field. Reputation accrues only through completed work, and a single ember of misbehavior, one proven fraud, burns the stake and the identity's history, so attackers pay real capital for every fake persona while honest agents keep their deposit and earn fees. The cost scales with the attack, not with honest participation.
